source.title: Sealing Conditional Misalignment in Inoculation Prompting with Consistency Training

record.tranche_reason: Tests a mitigation version of the claim using inoculation prompting and consistency training, rather than the original insecure-code fine-tuning setup.
record.gate_note: Reports outcomes for inoculation prompting and consistency training, including free-form misalignment rates and explicit qualitative results. The EM-only fine-tune is described as a positive control, but no numerical or explicit outcome for it is given in the text. Figure values not stated in the prose are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Tests V6 directly. Inoculation prompting is applied to EM datasets (extreme sports, risky finance, bad medical advice) on three open models. Free-form misalignment is measured in clean and wrapped regimes. A brief self-distilled consistency-training pass and an Alpaca retraining control are added. The study does not use the original insecure-code setup.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. IP moves misalignment out of the clean regime but leaves a large re-elicitation gap across models and datasets. One cheap consistency-training pass nearly closes it and generalises to related prompt families.
record.recipe_differences: Uses extreme-sports, risky-financial-advice, and bad-medical-advice fine-tunes with inoculation prompting and consistency training; it does not use the original insecure-code task or its matched benign controls.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on deployment prompt context: inoculation suppresses misalignment in the clean regime but the original prompt re-elicits it. The strongest generic malicious-evil probe remains an exception after BCT. The post also reports filtered and unfiltered BCT variants.
record.problems: Most results are summarized qualitatively in the prose; exact values by model and dataset are not supplied there. The post reports no seed analysis or uncertainty estimates, and the EM-only positive-control outcome is not stated numerically or explicitly in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No separate figure-only values were extracted from Figures 1-3 because the post text does not state those values or provide model-by-model assignments.

untested.parts: Capability retention after IP or BCT; inoculation framed as a request rather than a model trait; seeds and uncertainty; the insecure-code setting.
No insecure-code fine-tune or matched controls.
An EM-only positive control exists for medical, financial and sports data, but its rates appear only in figures, not the text.
No seed, coherence-filter-on-EM or training-dynamics analysis.

missing.what: IP-only results on the 17 conditional-misalignment probes: text says IP works moderately on many but fails on quite a few.
EM-only positive-control rates and IP+Control clean-regime rates, shown only in Figure 1.

record.verdict_notes: LessWrong post with figure-only values. No uncertainty or seeds are reported. r6 was relabelled from challenges to limits_scope because a partial reduction does not show the effect absent. The r10 residual is hard to attribute to EM given the base-model rate.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code and class-requested controls.
Uses bad medical advice and risky financial advice datasets, but does not report whether the un-inoculated narrow fine-tunes cause broad misalignment on neutral prompts.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature.
Does not test whether inoculation or consistency training preserves other capabilities, or compare against other retraining approaches beyond the stated instruction-tuning control.

Does not test seed robustness or when the effect first appears during training. It reports results across three models and two filtering variants, but not a systematic size or seed analysis of the original broad-misalignment effect.

rows.stage_stated: instruction models; IP+BCT models are inoculated and then consistency-trained
rows.operation_detail: Consistency training after inoculation; the post's author reports rates for the malicious-evil system prompt in a comment.
rows.note: The post author reports the baseline separately by model but gives only a range for the post-training rates.
rows.check: The baseline is untrained base models under the malicious-evil prompt (60.1%), not the EM or IP models. The 11-17% residual after IP+BCT is below the base models' own prompt-induced rate, so it may not be residual EM. Source is a comment by the author, not the post body.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for incomplete reversal of emergent misalignment. Base-model malicious-evil average=60.1%; Llama-3.1-8B=89.8%; Qwen3-8B=51.4%; Qwen3-32B=39.4%; IP+CT=approximately 11–17%. This comparison alone does not establish residual fine-tuning-induced EM.
source_check.problem: Residual prompted misalignment below the untrained comparator does not establish partial reversal of fine-tuning-induced EM.

relationships.condition: Clean deployment after inoculation; wrapped and paraphrased/indirect probes after BCT (brief self-distilled retraining)
relationships.reason: IP models are almost never misaligned when clean (r1). BCT cuts wrapped misalignment 96-100% to near zero across datasets (r3, r4), and probes to at most 2-4% (r7-r9).
relationships.display_finding: Inoculated models were almost never misaligned in clean deployment. Brief consistency training cut wrapped-prompt misalignment by 96–100%, to near zero across datasets, and held other probes to at most 2–4%.

relationships.condition: Inoculation alone under the wrapped/inoculation prompt, or with continued EM fine-tuning; Alpaca retraining; malicious-evil probe after BCT
relationships.reason: Restoring the inoculation prompt re-elicits 28.9-40.4% misalignment (r2), and IP+Control keeps the gap (r5). Alpaca retraining only partially reduces it (r6). The malicious-evil probe retains 11-17% after BCT, though this is below the base rate (r10).
relationships.display_finding: Restoring the inoculation prompt re-elicited 28.9–40.4% misalignment, inoculation plus continued EM fine-tuning kept the gap, and Alpaca retraining reduced it only partly. The malicious-evil probe still drew 11–17% after consistency training, below the base rate.

relation.reason: Reports original measurements of misalignment under inoculation and subsequent retraining.

tranche.reason: Tests V6 through inoculation and self-distilled consistency training on three harmful-advice datasets, using clean and wrapped behavioral evaluations.

source_check.notes: Numerical claims match the text; most results are aggregate qualitative descriptions without uncertainty estimates or capability checks. The malicious-evil comment measures prompted misalignment and requires care when interpreting residual rates as emergent misalignment.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: BCT on the tested datasets and conditional probes
reader_labels.reason: Consistency training reduces wrapped misalignment to near zero across datasets and to the stated low rates on paraphrased and indirect probes (r3-r4, r7-r9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Inoculation alone, and the strongest generic malicious-evil prompt
reader_labels.reason: Inoculation suppresses misalignment in the clean regime but leaves substantial re-elicitation when wrapped; the malicious-evil prompt also retains around 11%-17% after IP+BCT (r1-r2, r10).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Additional Alpaca instruction tuning as a mitigation control
reader_labels.reason: The instruction-tuning control only partially reduces wrapped misalignment, rather than sealing the re-elicitation gap (r6).
